title: RPX/RSI 1.1 An Exchange and Hardware-Interface Framework for Bounded Reflex Action, Structured Physical Observability and Cyber-Physical Containment
content: Physical and Spatial AI systems increasingly combine rich perception, learned world models and high-performance computing with actuators that must respond under strict timing, authority, safety and energy constraints. This Technical Note presents RPX/RSI 1.1, a technology-neutral framework that separates an urgent local reflex path from slower policy, inference and world-model functions. RPX defines transport-independent exchange semantics for compressed events, verified configuration, permission envelopes, bounded actions, security states and structured event-action traces. RSI defines the corresponding hardware or mixed-signal interface: sensor-near conditioning, low-bit event extraction, programmable condition-to-action logic, bounded outputs, measured-response inputs, verified configuration memory, independent fallback and built-in test. The integrated framework treats security and observability as part of the physical action contract. It requires critical updates to be authenticated, fresh, compatible, physically plausible, verified and atomically activated, while preserving a last-valid configuration after failure. It also records compact, cardinality-controlled traces that bind event, active rule and permission state, asserted action, latency, measured response and result without placing high-volume logging in the urgent path. A Spatial AI profile is specified in detail; battery and photovoltaic examples illustrate how the same architecture can govern bounded topology-changing actions in energy systems. The document positions RPX/RSI relative to reactive robotics, tiered control, runtime assurance, event-based sensing, secure update and energy-proportional computing, and defines a threat model, conformance classes, test vectors, limitations and a validation roadmap.
